descriptions.text: A catwalk lashed to a dead cell tower. The wind up here has edges. A jury-rigged radio spits numbers and then swallows them. Cinder Reach looks small enough to pity. West, the orchard glitters. East, a sentry's roof.
The radio has settled into a satisfied crackle. You have the word. The tower still wants to fall, but not today. West is glass. East is the watchtower.

steps.say: With the lens seated, the static sharpens until it is almost rude. A woman's voice, bored of surviving, says the clearance once: CINDER. Say it to the sentry. Do not embroider it.
Numbers. Then a syllable — cin — and the wind takes the rest. The lens from the orchard would make this a sentence.
Again. Cinder-something. A child's name used as a key. One more time and the tower may get tired of teasing you.
The third time the tower gives up. The word is CINDER. Say it plain to the woman with the rifle.
